artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

release_name_discogs: Intrigue (Steven Wilson Presents: Progressive Sounds In UK Alternative Music 1979-89)

perplexity.description:
Intrigue: Progressive Sounds In UK Alternative Music 1979–89 is a curated compilation assembled by musician and producer Steven Wilson, released in February 2023 by Demon Records. The collection comprises 58 tracks exploring the experimental and progressive dimensions of British alternative music during the 1980s, a decade often dismissed by progressive rock purists. Wilson's curation challenges the notion that ambitious, conceptually-driven music disappeared after punk's initial wave, instead highlighting artists who maintained experimental rigor within the alternative underground. The compilation features established acts including Wire, XTC, The Stranglers, Ultravox, Cocteau Twins, Kate Bush, and Tears for Fears, alongside more obscure figures like Dead Can Dance, Cardiacs, and No-Man.

The album spans multiple formats reflecting its scope: a comprehensive 4CD box set with an 80-page booklet containing extensive liner notes by James Nice and Wilson's introduction; a 7LP vinyl edition with 40 pages of documentation; and a condensed 2LP version featuring 20 highlights with a 12-page booklet. The mastering was handled by Phil Kinrade at AIR Mastering, ensuring sonic quality across the reissued material. Rather than presenting a chronological survey, the compilation emphasizes thematic connections between post-punk experimentalism, electronic innovation, and art-rock ambition, drawing from both mainstream alternative acts and deeper catalog cuts.

As a curatorial project within Wilson's discography, Intrigue represents his continued engagement with archival reissue work and historical reassessment, following similar projects remixing and remastering classic recordings. The compilation serves both as an introduction to 1980s British alternative music for newcomers and as a recontextualization for existing listeners, positioning the decade as a period of genuine creative ferment rather than commercial compromise.
